children: Coffee and cocoa futures posted net losses for the week after sharp gains in previous weeks, while sugar futures gained modestly.
There will be no trading for arabica coffee, raw sugar and New York cocoa futures on Monday due to the Labor Day holiday in the United States.
SUGAR
* Raw sugar
was little changed on Friday to close at 18.07 cents per lb. The market hit a 16-month peak of 18.77  cents on Wednesday. It ended the week with a 2.6% gain.
* Sugar production in top grower Brazil's key center-south region fell 7.9% in the first half of August, the agriculture ministry said.
* "As the US-Iran conflict continues to drag on, elevated energy prices will sustain incentives for Brazilian mills to prioritise ethanol production over sugar," said BMI, a unit of Fitch Solutions.
* Brazil exported 2.7 million metric tons of sugar in August, 27% less than a year ago.
* It added El Niño poses significant risks for sugar output in key growers India and Thailand.
* El Niño is set to intensify further into 2027 and could be the strongest ever, raising risks of extreme weather into next year, the World Meteorological Organization said.
* White sugar
settled down $3.50, or 0.7%, at $523.10 a ton.
COFFEE
* Arabica coffee
was little changed at $2.956 per lb, after hitting a five-week low of $2.8975 on Thursday. The market posted a 5.5% weekly loss.
* The contract is under pressure overall from a pick-up in top grower Brazil's exports and the return of rains to its coffee region.
* Brazil exported 45% more coffee in August than in the same month a year before, the government said on Friday. Shipments reached 3.44 million bags.
* Against that however, broker and consultant Michael Nugent pointed out: "We have genuinely tight arabica certified stocks, still-low inventories at destination (markets) and ... El Niño".
* Robusta coffee
settled up $56, or 1.7%, at $3,430 a ton, after hitting a 2-1/2-month low of $3,329 on Thursday.
COCOA
* London cocoa
was little changed at £4,518 per ton, remaining some way off Tuesday one-year high of £4,988. London cocoa lost 7% in the week.
* El Nino is a concern for cocoa, but broker ADMIS said these concerns have lessened somewhat.
* "The previous El Nino brought cool, wet weather during the late summer that cause(d) disease problems. So far this year at least, (West Africa) has avoided the pattern," it said.
* New York cocoa
rose 0.2% to $6,188 a ton. It also lost 7% weekly.
